packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
packet-04 - unverified image-only reading
Exposure statement: nothing in my context before viewing the images revealed a proposed identification or reading for this packet. The leaf itself carries a heading (see below) which I transcribe as seen.

LAYOUT SURVEY (image-001.jpg, reduced overview, one face)
- Single paper leaf, upright, photographed on black with colour chart (lower left) and cm scale (right edge). Leaf approx. 16 x 28 cm by the scale.
- Content is MUSIC NOTATION, not prose: hand-ruled five-line staves with mensural/early-modern round-headed notes (stems, flags), clefs at left of each staff, text underlay beneath each staff in a cursive humanistic hand (brown ink).
- Staves are grouped in systems of three staves (three braced/bracketed staves at the left margin): systems begin at approx. image y=240, y=510, y=820; ten staves total visible (3 + 3 + 3, plus the start of the top system). Each system has its own text underlay. Wide blank gaps between systems.
- Heading at top left (same or similar ink): "Magnificat 3a vocum" (tentative) followed by a parenthetical in a different, later-looking hand, and at top right a fragment of further text cut by the damaged edge.
- Modern pencil/ink shelf note under the heading: "Stams, STA, Frg. 14r" (tentative reading; modern archival annotation).
- A further faint later annotation (pencil?) between system 2 and system 3, approx. y=770-800, two lines, partly legible.
- Enlarged decorated initials begin each verse at the left of the first staff's underlay: "E" (system 1), "Q" (system 2), "F" (system 3).
- Repetition signs (a sign like "÷" or a tilde with dots, ij-type repeat marks) appear in the underlay.
- Damage: right edge torn and lost, with holes, especially at y=430-460, 520-640, 830-1000; a vertical tear/crack around x=1060-1080 in the bottom system. Upper right corner lost. Text at right margin is truncated.
- Only one overview face so far; I will check for further images.
- CORRECTION after viewing tile image-002 (overview image-001 still in view): the marks at the left of each staff are clefs (C-clef type with flat signature), not system braces. The underlay text runs continuously from one staff to the next ("spiritus meus" / "in Deo salutari meo"), so this is most likely a single voice-part written out staff after staff, grouped into verse sections separated by blank space (sections begin with the enlarged initials E, Q, F). Interpretation, not certain.
- The enlarged initials appear to be "E" preceded by a hatched/decorated letter (looks like a cadel "N"-shaped flourish attached to E), "Q", and "F".
- Sharp/natural signs drawn as an "x"-like mark with a tail appear BELOW some notes on staff 3 (image-002).

TRANSCRIPTION
Convention: line numbers count text lines (headings and underlay) from the top of each image; staves are noted but music is not transcribed. "÷" marks a repeat sign of the ij type as drawn.

image-002.jpg (native tile, top-left of leaf; overlaps image-001 top-left quadrant)
L1 (heading, main hand): Magnificat 3a(?) uocum   [the "3" carries a superscript abbreviation, read as "3a" or "3u"; "uocum" with tilde/stroke over final "m"? - tentative]
L1 (cont., different, greyer hand, cut at right edge of tile): (fran Stam[...]   [tentative; looks like a later annotation in parentheses]
L2 (modern annotation, cut at right): Sta[...]
  [staff 1: C-clef with flat at left; flat signature; notes]
L3 (underlay staff 1): [decorated initial, hatched] Et exultauit spiritusmeus   [written as "spiritusmeus" without space]
  [staff 2: clef, flat]
L4 (underlay staff 2): salutari meo          in Deo [continues beyond tile]
  [staff 3: clef; two "x"-shaped accidentals drawn below notes]
L5 (underlay staff 3): salutari me          o     salut[...]   [syllable "o" separated under its note: "me - o"]

image-003.jpg (native tile, top-right of leaf; overlaps image-002 on "in Deo" / "o" columns)
L1 (grey later hand, parenthetical, left cut): [...]n Stams?(?)[...])   [the parenthesis begun in image-002; reads roughly "(fran Stams..." - tentative; small superscript marks after it unclear]
L1 (top right corner, main hand, damaged edge with ink blot/hole before it): Cant[...]   [a capital C with flourish, then "ant"; edge torn after; likely a part label, tentative]
L2 (modern pencil): Stams, STA, Frg. 14r
  [staff 1, continuation]
L3 (underlay, overlap "[spiritus]meus" at left edge): [...]meus      Et exulta   uit Spiritus meus   [the word "exultauit" split "exulta - uit" under notes; final "s" of meus at torn edge]
  [staff 2]
L4 (underlay, overlap "in Deo"): in Deo salutari meo         salutari meo
  [staff 3: ends with a final note and then a custos/flourish and a large decorative double-stroke ending mark (end of section)]
L5 (underlay): salutari me o   [final "o" written under the flourish]
- Below staff 3 on this tile: blank paper, torn hole at right edge.

image-004.jpg (native tile, left middle of leaf; top overlaps image-002 last underlay line)
L1 (overlap with image-002 L5, not new text): salutari me   o   salut[...]
  [blank gap]
  [staff 4: clef + flat, opening rests, then notes; a rest/initial stroke at upper left of first notes]
L2 (underlay staff 4): [enlarged decorated initial Q, hatched, with flourish tail] uia fecit mihi magna   ["uia" begins immediately after the initial, i.e. Q-uia]
  [staff 5: clef + flat]
L3 (underlay staff 5, begins indented under mid-staff): mihi magna  [repeat sign: a long tilde-stroke with dots, "÷"/ij type]
  [staff 6: clef + flat]
L4 (underlay staff 6): po tens e(st)   [est written as e + abbreviation stroke/loop over "st"? - "e" with superscript mark]        et sanctu(m)? nomē (nomen) eiꝰ (eius)   ["sanctu" with superscript stroke - read "sanctum"; "eig"-shaped final = ei + us-sign]
  [below: a long descending stroke from final word, not a letter]
L5 (later grey pencil annotation, faint, cut at right): Fg 1966?(?) als Einband zu(?) P. K[...]ch(?), Germa[...]   [very tentative: "als Einband" fairly clear; rest uncertain]
L6 (same annotation, second line, cut): Am[...]

image-005.jpg (native tile, right middle of leaf; overlaps image-003 bottom and image-004 right half)
L1 (overlap with image-003 L5): salutari me o
  [blank gap; torn hole at right edge]
  [staff 4 continuation; notes run to torn edge]
L2 (underlay staff 4, overlap "magna"): [...]magna   [repeat sign ÷, long stroke with dots]          quia f[...]   [at torn right edge; "quia" clear, then "f" cut]
  [staff 5 continuation; small paper flap/stain mid-staff with reddish spot; notes partly over damaged area]
L3 (underlay staff 5): [repeat sign ÷]   mihi magna   [repeat sign ÷]          qui pote[...]   ["qui po" clear, then "te" cut at torn edge - tentative]
  [staff 6 continuation; last notes are longer values; edge torn]
L4 (underlay staff 6, overlap "nomē eiꝰ"): [...] nomē eiꝰ   [repeat sign ÷]          ei   [then at torn edge] ꝰ?/us[...]   [read "ei - us" split across notes, second syllable at edge, partly lost - tentative]
L5 (later grey pencil annotation, continuing image-004 L5): [...]i. Germania Inferior(?)   ["Germania" fairly clear; "Inferior" tentative]
L6 (same annotation): Amsterdam 1622   [date digits "1622" fairly clear; "Amsterdam" fairly clear]
- [see combined annotation note below]

image-006.jpg (native tile, bottom-left of leaf; top overlaps image-004 bottom)
L1 (overlap with image-004 L4, cut at top): po tens e(st)   et sanctu(m) nomē eiꝰ   [overlap only]
L2-L3 (overlap with image-004 L5-6, pencil annotation): Fg 1966?(?) als Einband zu(?) P. K[...], Germa[...] / Am[...]   [same faint pencil; still uncertain at "Fg 1966?" and "P. K...". Second word after "als" again looks like "Einband"]
  [staff 7: clef + flat; notes]
L4 (underlay staff 7): [enlarged initial F, decorated with knot below] Fecit potentiā (potentiam)   [a superscript stroke over final "a" - expansion "potentiam" tentative]   [repeat sign ÷]          feci[t ...]   [continues right]
  [staff 8: clef + flat]
L5 (underlay staff 8): in brachio ſuo          fecit po te[ntiam ...]   [continues right]
  [staff 9: clef + flat]
L6 (underlay staff 9): diſperſit ſuperbos  [a curved connecting stroke]  diſperſit   [continues right]
- Bottom margin of leaf below staff 9 is narrow; leaf edge visible; no further text on this tile.

image-007.jpg (native tile, bottom-right of leaf; overlaps image-005 bottom and image-006 right half)
L1 (overlap, cut at top): [...]nomē eiꝰ   [repeat stroke]   [further letters at top right cut off]
L2-L3 (overlap with image-005 L5-6, pencil): [...]i. Germania Inferior(?) / Amsterdam 1622
  [staff 7 continuation; large hole in staff right of centre; notes resume after hole]
L4 (underlay staff 7): fecit potentiam in brachio ſuo          in [b...]   [at torn right edge, "in" and start of next word cut]
  [staff 8 continuation; vertical crack through staff; small hole]
L5 (underlay staff 8, overlap "fecit po"): [f]ecit po tentiam   [long repeat/extension stroke crossing the crack]          in   [at right edge, "in" then cut]
  [staff 9 continuation; hole and brown stain at right]
L6 (underlay staff 9, overlap "dispersit"): diſperſit          diſperſit          diſperſit ſuperb[os]   [last word cut by torn edge after "superb"]
- Right edge: torn, text lost after the words noted; nothing else on this tile.

LAYOUT SURVEY, SECOND FACE (image-008.jpg, reduced overview)
- Same leaf, other side (pencil shelf note top right: "Stams, STA, Frg. 14v"). Torn edge now at LEFT (consistent with reverse of the recto's torn right edge). A plastic spatula/holder visible at lower right holding the leaf.
- Only the top third is written: three staves with underlay (staff tops approx. y=250, 345, 440), ending with a final flourish/double bar at right of staff 3. Below: blank, with ink show-through from the recto visible (mirror-image notes, initial Q faintly) and heavy brown staining in the lower third.
- Lower left corner: a pasted or adhering scrap of PRINTED paper showing reversed/inverted type ("...nus" etc., mirror or upside-down) - likely offset or residue from a binding use. Not part of the music.
- A vertical ruled line near the right edge (approx. x=1205) - a margin rule.
- (overview note follows; tile readings below supersede it) Underlay visible in the overview: "[...] esurientes(?) ... [repeat] ... esur[ientes]", "impleuit bonis   et diuites dimis[it]", "dimisit   inanes   inanes   inanes   dimisit inanes" - to be checked on tiles.

image-009.jpg (native tile, top-left of verso; torn left edge)
L1 (top-left torn scrap, main-hand ink, faded): [...]um   [only "um" (or "rum"/"cum") visible at edge of a projecting scrap; preceding letters lost - tentative]
  [staff 1: left end torn/stained (glossy residue, possibly adhesive), notes from x~400; beamed/ligated pair of notes with horizontal bar under stems at centre]
L2 (underlay staff 1, far left, faint, partly in stain): [...]er t[...]?   [faint "er" and a "t"-like letter with a red speck; very uncertain - may be underlay continuing from previous text or show-through]
L2 (cont.): Eſurientes   [initial "E" written large as a C-shaped form with inner stroke; final "s" with a hook]
  [staff 2: notes]
L3 (underlay staff 2): [repeat stroke ÷]   [repeat stroke ÷]          impleuit   [continues right; a long stroke from the following repeat sign overlaps the end of the word]
  [staff 3: left end torn with hole]
L4 (underlay staff 3): [...]es   Dimiſit          inanes          inanes          in[anes]   ["inanes" read with dotted i? spelled "inanes"; first "es" is end of a word cut by torn left edge]

image-010.jpg (native tile, top-right of verso; overlaps image-009 right side)
L1 (modern pencil, top right): Stams, STA, Frg. 14v
- A vertical ruled line (ink) runs top to bottom near the right edge, past which the staves end.
  [staff 1 continuation: flat above one note; beamed pair (overlap); near the end a stained/blotted group of notes, then a custos-like flourish crossing the margin rule]
L2 (underlay staff 1, overlap "[esurien]tes"): [...]tes   [repeat stroke ÷]          eſur   [then two small strokes "ıı" - possibly an ij repeat abbreviation; word not completed - tentative]
  [staff 2 continuation]
L3 (underlay staff 2): [i]mpleuit bonis          et diuites dimiſi[t]   ["impleuit bonis": a long thin stroke runs through "uit bo" - this looks like the tail of the preceding repeat sign drawn across the word, not a deletion, but it could be read as a strike-through; uncertain. "dimisit" squeezed at the margin, last letters at the rule]
  [staff 3 continuation; ends with a final note, then a large C-shaped flourish and terminal sign beyond the last notes (end of piece/section)]
L4 (underlay staff 3, overlap "[i]nanes"): [...]nes   inanes   [curved connecting stroke]   dimiſit inanes
- Note on "inanes" (this tile and image-009): the first letters are a run of minims without a clearly visible i-dot, so the word could equally be read "manes" as written; I give "inanes" as the minim reading, uncertain.
- Below staff 3: blank (show-through only) on this tile.

image-011.jpg (native tile, left middle of verso; top overlaps image-009 bottom)
L1 (overlap with image-009 L4, not new text): [...]es   Dimiſit   inanes   inanes   in[anes]
- Remainder of tile: no writing in this hand. Faint mirror-image notes and staff lines show through from the recto. Torn left edge with a glossy (adhesive?) patch; brown stains lower right; fibres/threads stuck to the surface lower left.

image-012.jpg (native tile, right middle of verso; top overlaps image-010 bottom)
L1 (overlap with image-010 L4, not new text): [...]nes   inanes   dimiſit inanes   [then a dot-like point below the end; the terminal flourish at staff end]
- Remainder: blank; mirror-image show-through of recto notes and the enlarged Q initial (reversed) visible. Margin rule continues down the right side.

image-013.jpg (native tile, bottom-left of verso)
- No music or handwriting. Torn left edge; a hole and a crack; fibres adhering at top left; large brown stain at right; a small blue mark.
- At lower left, an adhering scrap (or offset) of a different paper bearing PRINTED blackletter/gothic type, inverted relative to the leaf (letters read upside down and/or mirror-reversed). Visible letter groups, as seen (not rotated): line a "[...]wiq?" ; line b "[...]8nu[..] ı" ; line c (below a thin red horizontal rule) "[...]ꝺoʇ?" . Turned 180 degrees these would read roughly "...qim..." / "...nus r..." / "...tot?..." - all very tentative; three partial lines only, with a red rule (rubrication or printed rule) beneath the second line. This is not part of the music manuscript and is likely residue from the leaf's use in a binding.

image-014.jpg (native tile, bottom-right of verso)
- No writing. Faint show-through of recto notes; large brown stain; vertical margin rule near right edge; a vertical crease/fold line at centre; plastic holder at lower right. image-015 does not exist; packet ends at image-014.

SUMMARY OF CONNECTED UNDERLAY (as read, both faces; repeats as written, music not transcribed)
Recto (14r per pencil note), single voice part:
  Heading: Magnificat 3a(?) uocum ... Cant[...] (top right, damaged)
  Section 1 (initial E): Et exultauit spiritusmeus / Et exulta-uit Spiritus meus / [?] salutari meo / in Deo salutari meo / salutari meo / salutari me-o / salutari me-o [section end flourish]
  Section 2 (initial Q): Q-uia fecit mihi magna ÷ / quia f[ecit ...] / ÷ mihi magna ÷ / mihi magna ÷ / qui pote[...] / po-tens e(st) / et sanctu(m) nomē (nomen) eiꝰ (eius) ÷ / ei-[us] (edge)
  Section 3 (initial F): Fecit potentiā(m) ÷ / fecit potentiam in brachio ſuo / in [b...] (edge) / in brachio ſuo / fecit po-tentiam ÷ / in (edge) / diſperſit ſuperbos / diſperſit / diſperſit / diſperſit / diſperſit ſuperb[os] (edge)
Verso (14v), three staves only:
  [...]um (top-left scrap) / [...]er t[...]? (faint) / Eſurientes ÷ / eſur [ıı?] / ÷ ÷ / impleuit bonis / et diuites dimiſi[t] / [...]es Dimiſit / inanes / inanes / in[anes] / inanes / dimiſit inanes [final flourish]
  Note: on the verso the right-hand ends of lines are complete (margin rule) but the left ends are torn; between "diſperſit ſuperb[os]" at the foot of the recto and "Eſurientes" at the top of the verso, intervening text is not on this leaf as far as visible (the verso top-left scrap "[...]um" and faint "[...]er t[...]" may be its last remnant).

LIMITATIONS
- Music notation not transcribed; only underlay text and annotations.
- Recto right edge and verso left edge torn: words at those edges are partial ("quia f[...]", "qui pote[...]", "ei[us]", "in [b...]", "superb[os]", "in[anes]", "Cant[...]").
- "inanes" vs "manes": minim strokes without a clear i-dot; ambiguous as written.
- Heading superscript after "3" (3a/3u) and the grey parenthetical "(fran Stams...?)" are uncertain.
- Modern pencil annotations (shelfmark "Stams, STA, Frg. 14r/14v"; "... als Einband ... Germania Inferior(?) Amsterdam 1622") are transcribed tentatively and are not part of the original text.
- Printed scrap on verso lower left read only as inverted letter groups; not rotated or cropped.
- No crops made; no contrast adjustments. Nothing done beyond the brief's rules. The underlay is a familiar liturgical text, which I recognise by its content, but I transcribed only what is visible and did not fill gaps from memory; no proposed identification was supplied in my context.

- Combined annotation reading (image-004 L5-6 + image-005 L5-6), tentative: "Fg 1966? als Einband zu P. K[...], Germania Inferior, Amsterdam 1622" - i.e. a modern note apparently recording the fragment's use as a binding for a printed book; not part of the music text.
